newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Commission calls vets to review BSE sheep proposal.
newsitem.headline: Commission calls vets to review BSE sheep proposal.

text.p: The European Commission has called a meeting of senior EU veterinary officials on November 29 to review plans to ban the use of suspect sheep tissue in human and animal food, a spokesman said.

"Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler has called a special meeting to renconsider the proposal," Commission agriculture spokesman Gerard Kiely said, referring to the EU's Standing Veterinary Committee of member state officials.

The Commission proposed in July to ban the use of sheep brains, spleens and spinal cords in a precautionary move to protect human health after British and French reports that sheep could catch Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy (BSE) -- mad cow disease.
Sheep have long been known to suffer from scrapie, a widespread brain-wasting disease similar to BSE.

But the proposal was shelved after only Britain, France and Ireland showed any support for the idea. Other countries argued that such measures were economically unjustified, saying there was only a slight health risk.
"It's difficult to understand the reluctance of member states since they all say that the protection of public health must come first," Kiely said.
Experts were unsure that the BSE agent could be totally eradicated by heat and chemical processing of sheep parts, he added.
In a separate move, the Commission has written to the European Parliament's BSE committee of inquiry asking it to invite the chairmen of the EU's BSE advisory committees to testify before it.
These are the chairmen of the Scientific Veterinary Committee, Scientific Committee on Foodstuffs, Cosmetics Committee and BSE sub-group.

"This request is made for reasons of objectivity, transparency and fairness," Commission Secretary General David Williamson said in the letter released to the press. -- Brussels Newsroom 32 2 287 6800
